newsitem.title: UK: Job losses feared at Guinness distilleries.
newsitem.headline: Job losses feared at Guinness distilleries.

text.p: EDINBURGH, May 14, Reuter - Union leaders meet officials on Wednesday at United Distillers, the spirits division of Guinness, to voice concerns over threatened job losses if the proposed merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan goes through.
United Distillers key brands include Johnnie Walker, Bell's, Gordon's Gin and Tanqueray Gin.

Staff throughout Scotland are braced for significant job cuts if the 24 billion stg merger to create GMG Brands is allowed to go through by monopoly authorities as expected. UD has 50 sites in Scotland employing around 4,000 people.

Ian Fulton, Scottish regional officer of the Manufacturing, Science and Finance Union said: "We need to discuss a range of issues including plant configurations, staffing levels and employment security."
Guinness chairman Tony Greener said on Monday the merger is likely to lead to around 2,000 job cuts from the merged group's 85,000-strong combined workforce.

UD employs 200 people at its headquarers in Edinburgh and a further 300 in sales and marketing in Perth. At Glasgow an export centre employs 150 staff and a total of 1,150 people work at three packaging and bottling plants in Leven, Glasgow and Kilmarnock.
UD also has 27 Scottish malt distilleries from Aberfeldy to Talisker and two grain distilleries. A further 600 staff are employed in cooperage and warehousing at Alloa.
GrandMet has four malt distilleries in Scotland, all in the highlands at Auchroisk, Glen Spey, Knockando and Strathmill. Sales and marketting staff are based at the firm's J&B plant at Dumbarton.
